definition_zh: adj. 令人敬畏的；引起惊叹的；（口语）极好的；了不起的
definition_en: Inspiring awe, wonder or fear; in informal use, extremely good or impressive.
core_image: 站在崖边一时说不出话的那种震动
scene: 峡谷边缘风很大，孩子们一时都说不出话。The view from the canyon rim was awesome, and the children fell silent.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：awesome 指景象或力量宏大得令人敬畏，带有震动与肃然之意。

collocations.zh: 重大得令人敬畏的责任

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Inspiring awe
senses.definition: so large, powerful or grand that it fills a person with wonder mixed with fear
senses.definitionCN: 宏大、有力或壮丽到让人既惊叹又心生畏惧
senses.example: The storm showed the awesome force of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 那场风暴显示了海洋令人敬畏的力量。
senses.why: Awesome is awe plus -some, so it describes whatever produces awe, a feeling older than admiration.
senses.whyCN: awesome 是 awe 加 -some，因此它描述任何能引出敬畏之物，而敬畏这种感受比欣赏更古老。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: in informal speech, very good or impressive, with the fear drained out of the original sense
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中指非常好或很出色，原义中的畏惧已被抽掉
senses.example: That was an awesome concert.
senses.exampleCN: 那场音乐会太棒了。
senses.why: Young speakers kept the intensity but dropped the dread, so a word for terror became a word of praise.
senses.whyCN: 年轻使用者保留了强度却舍去了畏惧，于是一个表恐惧的词变成了赞美词。

intro.en: Awesome is awe plus -some; awe comes from Old Norse agi, terror, which replaced an older English word for fear of the divine.
intro.cn: awesome 是 awe 加 -some；awe 来自古诺斯语 agi「恐惧」，它取代了更早的英语中表示对神明畏惧的词。

items.en: A root meaning to be anxious or choked lies behind words of dread and narrowness.
items.cn: 一个表示「焦虑、窒息」的词根支撑着恐惧与狭窄类的词。

items.en: Old Norse agi meant terror or discipline, the fear that keeps a person in order.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 agi 意为「恐惧、约束」，即使人守规矩的那种怕。

items.en: Northern Middle English took the word as aghe, dread of God or of a lord.
items.cn: 北部中古英语借作 aghe，指对神或领主的畏惧。

items.en: The form settled as awe, and the phrase stand in awe kept the older fear.
items.cn: 形式定为 awe，而表示肃然敬畏的短语保留了更早的畏惧义。

items.en: English added -some in the 1590s to describe what inspires that dread.
items.cn: 英语在 1590 年代加上 -some，用来描述引出这种畏惧之物。

items.en: American youth speech from the 1960s turned awesome into general praise.
items.cn: 1960 年代起的美国青年口语把 awesome 变成泛用的赞美词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the awe family, including the cousin that went bad; the near-meaning group lists words for grand and for excellent.
note.cn: 形近组保留 awe 词族，包括那个走坏方向的近亲；近义组列出表示宏大与表示极好的词。

entries.definitionCN: 被 sudden 惊叹震住的。

entries.definition: So striking it stops the breath.

normalIntro.en: Awesome is awe plus -some: full of awe, whether that awe is dread at a cliff or delight at a concert.
normalIntro.cn: awesome 是 awe 加 -some：充满敬畏，无论是在崖边的震慑还是在音乐会的兴奋。

normal.en: Awe once meant fear, not admiration.
normal.cn: awe 早先指畏惧，不是欣赏。

normal.en: Awful took the bad road, awesome the good.
normal.cn: awful 走了坏的方向，awesome 走了好的方向。

normal.en: Formal writing keeps the grand sense.
normal.cn: 正式书面语保留宏大之义。

normal.en: Speech uses it as general praise.
normal.cn: 口语把它当作泛用赞美。

normal.en: The noun phrase is stand in awe of.
normal.cn: 名词短语是 stand in awe of。

abstract.en: Picture a rim where words fail you.
abstract.cn: 想象一处让你说不出话的崖边。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave taller than the boat.
abstract.cn: 想象一道比船还高的浪。

abstract.en: Think of applause that starts before thought.
abstract.cn: 想象先于思考爆发的掌声。

examples.en: The cathedral has an awesome silence.
examples.cn: 那座大教堂有一种令人肃然的静。

examples.en: They faced an awesome task.
examples.cn: 他们面对一项艰巨得令人敬畏的任务。

examples.en: Your new bike looks awesome.
examples.cn: 你的新自行车看起来太棒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：awe「敬畏」+ -some「充满……的」——充满敬畏的，就是 awesome；口语里畏惧褪去，只剩「太棒了」。

root: 古诺斯语 agi「恐惧」入中古英语作 awe「敬畏」；1590 年代加 -some 成 awesome「令人敬畏的」，1960 年代美国口语又把它转为「极好的」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same shock of scale: the grand thing that silences you, and the good thing that makes you shout.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种体量带来的震动：让你沉默的宏大之物，与让你喊出来的美好之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at a cliff edge with no words left
core.cn: 核心意象：站在崖边一时说不出话的那种震动

branches.en: A canyon rim that silences children.
branches.cn: 让孩子沉默的峡谷边缘。

branches.en: The force of the sea in a storm.
A new bike praised on sight.
branches.cn: 一眼就被夸的新自行车。

branches.en: Both name a shock, one sober and one glad.
branches.cn: 两者都指震动，一者肃然，一者欣喜。

intro.en: Awesome is awe plus -some; the same -some builds handsome and lonesome, while -ful gives the darker cousin awful.
intro.cn: awesome 是 awe 加 -some；同一 -some 还构成 handsome 与 lonesome，而 -ful 则给出走向阴暗的近亲 awful。

latinIntro.en: The base is Norse rather than Latin; Latin magnus, great, supplies magnificent beside it, and timere, to fear, gives timid.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属诺斯语而非拉丁语；旁边的拉丁语 magnus「大」提供 magnificent，timere「畏惧」产生 timid。

definition_zh: 可怕的；糟糕的；非常的
definition_en: very bad or unpleasant, or causing fear
core_image: 天空压下一片黑云，雷声在头顶炸开
scene: 山顶的风突然停了。An awful silence followed the thunder.
sceneCN: 这里 awful 是「可怕的」（第 1 个义项：令人恐惧或震撼的）；句意是雷声过后是一片可怕的寂静。

pos.zh: 形容词：可怕的；糟糕的；非常的

derivatives.zh: 由 awful 加 -ly 构成，义为「非常；糟糕地」
由 awful 加 -ness 构成，义为「糟糕；可怕」
基础词，义为「敬畏」，awful 由其加 -ful 构成

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: very bad and frightening
senses.definitionCN: 非常糟糕且令人害怕的
senses.example: An awful silence followed the thunder.
senses.exampleCN: 雷声过后是一片可怕的寂静。
senses.why: Awful first meant 'full of awe', and awe was a mixture of fear and wonder, so the word began with terror rather than mere badness.
senses.whyCN: awful 最初意为「充满敬畏的」，而敬畏混杂着恐惧与惊叹，所以这个词起初指恐怖，而不只是「差」。

senses.title: Very bad
senses.definition: extremely unpleasant or of poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 令人很不愉快或质量很差的
senses.example: The weather was awful all week.
senses.exampleCN: 整个星期天气都很糟糕。
senses.why: As awe weakened in everyday speech, awful slid from terror to ordinary dislike, which is the sense most people use today.
senses.whyCN: 随着 awe 在日常口语中减弱，awful 从恐怖滑向普通的厌恶，这就是今天最常用的义项。

senses.title: Very great in amount
senses.definition: used to emphasize a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调数量很大
senses.example: It took an awful lot of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这花了非常多功夫。
senses.why: Something frightening is also overwhelming, so awful became an intensifier for size and degree.
senses.whyCN: 令人害怕的东西也让人招架不住，于是 awful 变成强调数量与程度的词。

intro.en: Awful is a word that fell from awe to mere dislike.
intro.cn: awful 是一个从敬畏跌落到单纯厌恶的词。

items.en: ege meant 'fear'.
items.cn: ege 意为「恐惧」。

items.en: awe meant fear mixed with wonder.
items.cn: awe 意为恐惧混杂惊叹。

items.en: aweful meant 'full of awe'.
items.cn: aweful 意为「充满敬畏的」。

items.en: awful meant 'frightful'.
items.cn: awful 意为「可怕的」。

items.en: It weakened to 'very bad'.
items.cn: 后来弱化为「很糟的」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the awe base; the near-meaning group gives degrees of badness.
note.cn: 形近组都含 awe 词基；近义组是表示糟糕程度的词。

entries.definition: very, or in a bad way

normalIntro.en: Awful still carries the shadow of awe, even when it only means bad.
normalIntro.cn: 即使只表示「糟」，awful 仍带着敬畏的影子。

normal.en: Awful is stronger than bad but weaker than terrifying.
normal.cn: awful 比 bad 强，但比 terrifying 弱。

normal.en: An awful lot means a very large amount.
normal.cn: an awful lot 意为非常多。

normal.en: The adverb is awfully, not awful.
normal.cn: 副词是 awfully。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: AWE-ful.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the w from awe.
normal.cn: 拼写保留了 awe 中的 w。

abstract.en: See a black cloud pressing down before thunder.
abstract.cn: 想象雷声前压下来的黑云。

abstract.en: See a whole field bent flat by wind.
abstract.cn: 想象整片田野被风吹得贴地。

abstract.en: See a crowd frozen by one loud crack.
abstract.cn: 想象一声巨响让整个人群僵住。

examples.en: An awful silence followed the thunder.
examples.cn: 雷声过后是一片可怕的寂静。

examples.en: The weather was awful all week.
examples.cn: 整个星期天气都很糟糕。

examples.en: It took an awful lot of work.
examples.cn: 这花了非常多功夫。

dict_mnemonic.text: awe（敬畏）加 -ful（充满）：满心敬畏，先是怕，后来变成嫌它糟。

root: 由 awe「敬畏」加 -ful「充满」构成，awe 源自古英语 ege「恐惧」并受古诺斯语 agi 影响；由「令人敬畏的」弱化为「可怕的、糟糕的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fear, dislike and sheer size are the three stops on the road from awe to awful.
sensesIntro.cn: 恐惧、厌恶与量太大，是 awful 从敬畏一路走来的三站。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black cloud pressing down before thunder.
core.cn: 核心意象：雷声前压下来的黑云。

intro.en: The -ful suffix means 'full of', as in awful and hopeful.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为「充满」，如 awful 与 hopeful。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这一族词来自日耳曼语。

items.meaning: in an awful way, or very

definition_zh: 尴尬的；笨拙的；难对付的
definition_en: causing embarrassment, or moving in a clumsy way
core_image: 两只手都不知该往哪儿放，站在门口进退不得
scene: 礼堂里忽然安静下来。He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
sceneCN: 这里 awkward 是「尴尬的」（第 1 个义项：令人不自在、难为情的）；句意是他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。

pos.zh: 形容词：尴尬的；笨拙的；难对付的

derivatives.zh: 由 awkward 加 -ly 构成，义为「尴尬地；笨拙地」
由 awkward 加 -ness 构成，义为「尴尬；笨拙」

senses.title: Causing embarrassment
senses.definition: causing embarrassment or making people uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 令人难为情或让人不自在的
senses.example: He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。
senses.why: Awkward comes from Old Norse afugr, turned the wrong way, so the core image is something facing backwards and out of place.
senses.whyCN: awkward 来自古诺斯语 afugr「方向转反了」，核心意象是东西朝反了、位置不对。

senses.title: Clumsy in movement
senses.definition: moving or behaving in a clumsy way
senses.definitionCN: 动作或举止笨拙的
senses.example: The puppy was awkward on the smooth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 小狗在光滑的地板上走得很笨拙。
senses.why: A body facing the wrong way moves badly, so the same word names physical clumsiness.
senses.whyCN: 身体朝向不对就动得别扭，于是同一个词也指身体上的笨拙。

senses.title: Hard to deal with
senses.definition: difficult to use, handle or deal with
senses.definitionCN: 难以使用、处理或应付的
senses.example: The box was awkward to carry up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子很难搬上楼。
senses.why: Anything that does not fit the situation is hard to handle, which extends the word from people to objects and timing.
senses.whyCN: 任何与情境不合的东西都难对付，这就把词从人扩展到物品与时机。

intro.en: Awkward is a word about facing the wrong way.
intro.cn: awkward 说的是方向转反了。

items.en: afugr meant 'turned the wrong way'.
items.cn: afugr 意为「方向转反的」。

items.en: afugligr meant 'unfavourable'.
items.cn: afugligr 意为「不顺的」。

items.en: aukeward meant 'backhanded'.
items.cn: aukeward 意为「反手的」。

items.en: awkward meant 'clumsy'.
items.cn: awkward 意为「笨拙的」。

items.en: It also means socially embarrassing.
items.cn: 如今也指社交上的尴尬。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aw opening; the near-meaning group gives clumsiness and unease.
note.cn: 形近组都以 aw 开头；近义组是表示笨拙与不自在的词。

normalIntro.en: Awkward is the feeling of standing at the wrong angle to everything.
normalIntro.cn: awkward 是与一切都对不上角度的感觉。

normal.en: Awkward describes both people and situations.
normal.cn: awkward 既能形容人，也能形容处境。

normal.en: An awkward silence is a silence nobody can fill.
normal.cn: an awkward silence 是没人接得上的沉默。

normal.en: The adverb is awkwardly.
normal.cn: 副词是 awkwardly。

normal.en: The w in the middle is pronounced.
normal.cn: 中间的 w 要发音。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AWK-ward.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See two hands hovering with nowhere to rest.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手悬着，不知往哪放。

abstract.en: See a guest stuck between two open doors.
abstract.cn: 想象客人卡在两扇打开的门之间。

abstract.en: See a chair turned against the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子背对着桌子。

examples.en: He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
examples.cn: 他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。

examples.en: The puppy was awkward on the smooth floor.
examples.cn: 小狗在光滑的地板上走得很笨拙。

examples.en: The box was awkward to carry up the stairs.
examples.cn: 这个箱子很难搬上楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: awk 加 ward（朝向）：方向反着来，人就站得别扭，手脚也不听使唤。

root: 来自古诺斯语 afugr「方向转反的」，其派生 afugligr「不顺的」经中古英语 aukeward「反手的」进入英语；由「方向不对」引申为笨拙与尴尬。

sensesIntro.en: Wrong direction, clumsy body and difficult situation are the same misfit seen three ways.
sensesIntro.cn: 方向不对、动作笨拙与处境难办，是同一个「不合位」的三种看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands hovering with nowhere to rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手悬着，不知往哪放。

intro.en: The -ward suffix marks direction, as in awkward, backward and forward.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ward 标记方向，如 awkward、backward 与 forward。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word came from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古诺斯语。

definition_zh: 轴；轴线；中心线；联盟轴心
definition_en: an imaginary line about which a body turns; a central line or alliance
core_image: 陀螺上那根看不见的线：整团旋转都围着它
scene: 地理课上老师转动地球仪，指尖点着南北极的连线。The earth spins on its axis once a day.
sceneCN: 这里 axis 指「自转轴」（第 1 个义项：旋转所围绕的线）；句意：地球每天绕轴自转一周。

derivatives.zh: 公理（拼写相关但词源不同，仅形近提示）

senses.title: The line a spinning body turns about
senses.definition: an imaginary straight line around which a rotating body turns
senses.definitionCN: 旋转体绕之转动的假想直线
senses.example: The planet tilts on its axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗行星的自转轴是倾斜的。
senses.why: Latin axis named the axle of a wheel; every wheel implies its invisible line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 axis 本指车轮的轴；有轮必有那条无形的线。

senses.title: A reference line in graphs
senses.definition: a fixed reference line for measuring coordinates on a graph
senses.definitionCN: 坐标图上作度量基准的固定直线
senses.example: Plot cost on the vertical axis.
senses.exampleCN: 把成本标在纵轴上。
senses.why: A graph freezes rotation into a measuring line: the axle becomes a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 坐标图把旋转抽象成度量线：轮轴化为标尺。

senses.title: A central line of a body or structure
senses.definition: a real or imaginary central line of symmetry in a body, building, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 身体、建筑或规划中真实或假想的中心对称线
senses.example: The garden is laid out along a central axis.
senses.exampleCN: 花园沿中轴线布局。
senses.why: What everything is arranged around is still the axle idea, made architectural.
senses.whyCN: 万物环绕之线仍是轮轴意象的建筑化。

senses.title: An alliance between powers
senses.definition: a political alliance around which other powers group, as the Axis powers
senses.definitionCN: 以某方为核心的联盟，如轴心国
senses.example: The Axis powers were defeated in 1945.
senses.exampleCN: 轴心国于 1945 年战败。
senses.why: Mussolini spoke of an axis between Rome and Berlin: a line other states were to revolve around.
senses.whyCN: 墨索里尼称罗马与柏林之间有条「轴」，他国应绕之旋转。

senses.title: The second cervical vertebra
senses.definition: the second cervical vertebra on which the head rotates
senses.definitionCN: 头部赖以转动的第二颈椎
senses.example: The axis allows the head to turn side to side.
senses.exampleCN: 枢椎使头部得以左右转动。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the wheel word for the vertebra the head pivots on.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借轮轴之词命名头部转动的椎骨。

senses.title: A deer of the spotted kind
senses.definition: a small Asian deer with a spotted coat, the axis deer
senses.definitionCN: 产于亚洲的梅花点小鹿，称 axis deer
senses.example: Axis deer graze at the forest edge.
senses.exampleCN: 轴鹿在林缘吃草。
senses.why: The deer's name is a separate Latin word axis, a spotted Hindoo deer of old texts.
senses.whyCN: 此鹿名为拉丁语另一词 axis，古籍中的点斑鹿，与「轴」无关。

senses.title: In crystallography and optics
senses.definition: a principal direction in a crystal along which light or structure is measured
senses.definitionCN: 晶体中测量光性或结构的主方向
senses.example: Quartz has three axes of symmetry.
senses.exampleCN: 石英有三条对称轴。
senses.why: Science extends the reference-line sense to any principal direction of measurement.
senses.whyCN: 科学把基准线义扩展到一切主测量方向。

senses.title: Plural axes in mathematics
senses.definition: the plural form used of several such lines
senses.definitionCN: 指多条此类直线的复数形式
senses.example: The diagram shows all three axes.
senses.exampleCN: 图中三条轴线全部画出。
senses.why: The plural keeps the Greek-style ending, like crisis to crises.
senses.whyCN: 复数保留希腊式词尾，如 crisis 变 crises。

intro.en: Latin axis, axle, goes back to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning to drive or urge, the same source as Greek axon and English axle.
intro.cn: 拉丁语 axis「轮轴」可溯至原始印欧语词根「驱赶、推动」，与希腊语 axon、英语 axle 同源。

items.en: The root ag- meant to drive, to move a thing by force.
items.cn: 词根 ag- 意为驱赶、用力移动。

items.en: A derivative aks- named the rod that drives a wheel: the axle.
items.cn: 派生 aks- 指驱动轮子的杆：车轴。

items.en: Latin axis meant the axle of a wheel or the North Pole axis of the heavens.
items.cn: 拉丁语 axis 指轮轴，亦指天球旋转的极轴。

items.en: Greek axon, axle, is the same word, and survives in biology.
items.cn: 希腊语 axon 同源，存于生物学「轴突」。

items.en: English took axis from Latin for the axle and soon for the celestial line.
items.cn: 英语 16 世纪借入 axis，先指轮轴，继而指天轴。

items.en: The graph, anatomy, and political senses grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 坐标轴、解剖与政治义成于十九、二十世纪。

note.en: Group one holds the axle family and look-alikes; group two holds the central-line field.
note.cn: 第一组收轮轴词族与形近词；第二组收「中心线」义场。

entries.definition: the rod a wheel turns on; the everyday cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 轮轴；axis 的日常同源词。

entries.definition: a nerve fiber; the Greek form of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 神经轴突；同一词的希腊形式。

entries.definition: a chopping tool; older spelling ax, no kin to axis.
entries.definitionCN: 斧子；与 axis 词源无关，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: the point on which something turns.
the central part of a wheel; a center of activity.
the outer edge, as against the central axis.

normalIntro.en: axis is the Latin axle: everything that turns, turns around it.
normalIntro.cn: axis 即拉丁语轮轴：一切旋转都绕它进行。

normal.en: Root: Latin axis, axle.
normal.cn: 词根：拉丁语 axis「轮轴」。

normal.en: Kin: axle and axon are the same word.
normal.cn: 同源：axle 与 axon 同出一词。

normal.en: Plural: axes, like crisis to crises.
normal.cn: 复数 axes，如 crisis 变 crises。

normal.en: Adjective: axial, as in axial tilt.
normal.cn: 形容词 axial，如 axial tilt「轴倾角」。

normal.en: Politics: the Rome–Berlin axis of the 1930s.
normal.cn: 政治：1930 年代的罗马—柏林轴心。

abstract.en: See the invisible line through the spinning top.
abstract.cn: 看陀螺中那根无形的线。

abstract.en: Axis is the still point the whirl pretends to own.
abstract.cn: axis 是旋转假装拥有的那个不动之点。

abstract.en: Picture planets strung on a silver rod.
abstract.cn: 想象行星串在一根银杆上。

examples.en: The gyroscope keeps steady as long as its axis stays fixed.
examples.cn: 只要轴向不变，陀螺仪就能保持稳定。

examples.en: Label the horizontal axis with the months of the year.
examples.cn: 给横轴标上月份。

examples.en: The two nations formed an axis against their neighbors.
examples.cn: 两国结成轴心以对抗邻国。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克西斯」——爱围着一条克（刻）好的线转，这条线就是轴

root: 出自拉丁语 axis「轮轴、极轴」，溯至原始印欧语词根 *ag-「驱动」的派生形式 *aks-；与希腊语 axon「轴突」、英语 axle「轮轴」同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run one line through wheel, graph, city plan, alliance, vertebra, deer, crystal, and the plural form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项贯穿一条线：车轮、坐标、城市布局、联盟、颈椎、鹿、晶体与复数形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the still line everything turns around.
core.cn: 核心意象：万物绕之旋转的那条不动的线。

branches.en: Wheel and vertebra share the pivot of motion.
branches.cn: 车轮与颈椎同享「转动枢点」。

branches.en: Graph and crystal use the line to measure.
branches.cn: 坐标与晶体都借这条线来度量。

branches.en: The city plan turns the line into symmetry.
branches.cn: 城市规划把这条线化作对称。

branches.en: Politics imagines states revolving on a line.
branches.cn: 政治想象各国绕一条线旋转。

branches.en: A second Latin word and the plural close the entry.
branches.cn: 另一拉丁词与复数形式收尾。

intro.en: The axis family is small and old: a single Indo-European root gives the Latin, Greek, and English axle words.
intro.cn: axis 词族小而古老：一个印欧词根生出拉丁、希腊与英语的轮轴词。

latinIntro.en: Latin kin are direct: axis itself and its derivatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词直接：axis 本词及其派生。

items.meaning: rod on which a wheel turns

latinEntries.meaning: axle of a wheel; polar line of the heavens

latinEntries.meaningCN: 腋；后成 axillary（仅形近，词源不同支）

definition_zh: n. 车轴；轮轴；（连着车轮的）轴总成
definition_en: A rod or spindle on which a wheel turns, or the whole assembly joining two wheels of a vehicle.
core_image: 穿过轮心让轮子转起来的那根铁杆
scene: 修车师傅说后轴漏油，得整套换掉。The mechanic said the rear axle was leaking oil and had to be replaced.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：axle 指穿过轮心、让车轮绕之转动的那根杆或轴。

senses.title: The rod a wheel turns on
senses.definition: a rod or spindle passing through the centre of a wheel so that the wheel can rotate
senses.definitionCN: 穿过轮心的杆或轴，使车轮能够旋转
senses.example: The wheel spun freely on its axle.
senses.exampleCN: 车轮在轴上自由转动。
senses.why: Axle descends from a Norse word for the same rod, kin to axis, so the core is always the line a thing turns about.
senses.whyCN: axle 出自指同一根杆的诺斯语词，与 axis 同源，因此核心始终是「物体绕之转动的那条线」。

senses.title: The whole wheel assembly
senses.definition: in vehicle work, the shaft together with its bearings and the two wheels it carries
senses.definitionCN: 在车辆维修中，指轴连同轴承及其所带动的两个车轮
senses.example: They replaced the axle after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞后他们更换了整个轮轴总成。
senses.why: Because the rod is never found bare on a car, the name spread to the whole unit a mechanic removes.
senses.whyCN: 因为在汽车上这根杆从不单独存在，这个名称便扩展到修车师傅整体拆下的那个部件。

intro.en: Axle comes from Old Norse oxull, axle, from a Germanic root also behind axis and the Old English eax, all meaning the line a wheel turns on.
intro.cn: axle 来自古诺斯语 oxull「车轴」，出自同一日耳曼词根，axis 与古英语 eax 亦由此而来，都指车轮绕之转动的那条线。

items.en: A root meaning axle or shoulder joint gave words for the pivot a limb or wheel turns on.
items.cn: 一个表示「轴、肩关节」的词根产生了肢体或车轮绕之转动的枢轴类词。

items.en: Latin axis named an axle and also the line of the heavens, giving English axis.
items.cn: 拉丁语 axis 既指车轴，也指天球的轴线，产生英语 axis。

items.en: Old English eax meant axle, the native form that later lost ground.
items.cn: 古英语 eax 意为「车轴」，是后来退让的本族形式。

items.en: Old Norse oxull named the same rod and supplied the northern English form.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 oxull 指同一根杆，提供了英格兰北部的形式。

items.en: Middle English axeltre named the beam joining two wheels, from oxull plus tre, tree or beam.
items.cn: 中古英语 axeltre 指连接两轮的横梁，由 oxull 加 tre「木、梁」构成。

items.en: The shorter axle is recorded from the seventeenth century and became the workshop word.
items.cn: 较短的 axle 自十七世纪有记载，成为车间用语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the axis family; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring parts of a wheel assembly.
note.cn: 形近组保留 axis 词族；近义组列出轮轴总成上相邻的部件。

entries.definition: The line a body turns about.
A skating jump named after a man.
entries.definitionCN: 以人名命名的滑冰跳跃。

entries.definition: A passage between rows of seats.
A part that lets a shaft turn.

normalIntro.en: Axle is kin to axis: the line a wheel turns on, and then the whole unit built around that line.
normalIntro.cn: axle 与 axis 同源：车轮绕之转动的那条线，进而指围绕这条线造出的整个部件。

normal.en: Rear axle and front axle are the usual pairs.
normal.cn: rear axle 与 front axle 是常见的一对。

normal.en: Axle grease is a set workshop phrase.
normal.cn: axle grease 是固定车间用语。

normal.en: Axis is the line, axle is the part.
normal.cn: axis 是那条线，axle 是那个件。

normal.en: The plural is axles, not axies.
normal.cn: 复数是 axles，不是 axies。

normal.en: Axletree is the older, longer name.
normal.cn: axletree 是更早、更长的名称。

abstract.en: Picture an iron rod through a wooden wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铁杆穿过木轮。

abstract.en: Imagine the wheel spinning while the rod stays.
abstract.cn: 想象轮在转而杆不动。

abstract.en: Think of one beam carrying two wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横梁带动两个轮子。

examples.en: Grease the axle before the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途行驶前给车轴上润滑脂。

examples.en: The front axle took the whole impact.
examples.cn: 前轴承受了全部撞击。

examples.en: Both axles were bent beyond repair.
examples.cn: 两根车轴都弯得无法修复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ax（与 axis 同族，「轴」）+ -le「小部件」——穿过轮心的那根轴杆，就是 axle。

root: 印欧词根表「轴、枢轴」，拉丁语 axis 与古英语 eax 由此而来；古诺斯语 oxull 加 tre「梁」成中古英语 axeltre，十七世纪缩为 axle。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses centre on one turning line: the rod itself, and the whole assembly a workshop lifts out around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都围绕一条转动之线：杆本身，以及车间围绕它整体吊出的那套部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron rod through the wheel heart that lets it spin
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过轮心让轮子转起来的那根铁杆

branches.en: A wheel spinning on its rod.
A rear unit replaced after a crash.
branches.cn: 碰撞后更换的后轴总成。
弯得无法修复的两套总成。

branches.en: Both are built about one turning line.
branches.cn: 两者都围绕一条转动之线构成。

intro.en: Axle is ax plus the tool ending -le; the same ax root gives axis and axial, while -tree marked the older beam.
intro.cn: axle 是 ax 加工具词尾 -le；同一 ax 词根产生 axis 与 axial，而 -tree 标记了更早的横梁。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is axis, axle or heavenly line; Greek axon gives the same idea, and Latin rota, wheel, gives rotate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 axis「车轴、天轴」；希腊语 axon 给出同一概念，拉丁语 rota「轮」产生 rotate。

latinEntries.exampleCN: axon 给出生物学中的轴突。

definition_zh: v. 临时照看小孩（父母外出时）；引申指细心看护需要照料之事
definition_en: To look after a child while its parents are out; by extension, to watch over something that needs careful attention.
core_image: 父母出门后守在摇篮边的那几个小时
scene: 她答应周六晚上替邻居看孩子。She agreed to babysit for the neighbours on Saturday night.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：babysit 指在父母外出期间临时照看小孩。

derivatives.zh: 临时照看孩子这份工作

senses.title: Mind a child for a while
senses.definition: to care for a child in its own home during the absence of its parents
senses.definitionCN: 在父母不在时于孩子家中照料孩子
senses.example: He babysat for his sister twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周替姐姐看两次孩子。
senses.why: The word was formed backwards from babysitter, so it literally means to sit by a baby.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是由 babysitter 反向构出的，因此字面就是「坐在婴儿旁边」。

senses.title: Watch over something fragile
senses.titleCN: 看护需要细心照料之事
senses.definition: by extension, to give close, patient attention to a task or thing that cannot be left alone
senses.definitionCN: 引申指对不能放任不管的任务或事物给予细致耐心的关注
senses.example: Someone has to babysit the server all night.
senses.exampleCN: 得有人整夜盯着那台服务器。
senses.why: The child picture carries the idea of constant watching, so the verb spread to any job needing a nurse.
senses.whyCN: 看孩子的画面带着「持续守望」之意，于是这个动词扩展到任何需要看护的工作。

intro.en: Babysit is a back-formation from babysitter, recorded in the 1930s; baby is a nursery word and sit is native English, so the verb means to sit by a baby.
intro.cn: babysit 是由 babysitter 反向构词而来，1930 年代有记载；baby 是育儿用语，sit 是英语本族词，因此这个动词意为「坐在婴儿旁边」。

items.en: Babe was a nursery word for an infant, imitating early speech sounds.
items.cn: babe 是指婴儿的育儿用语，模仿早期语音。

items.en: Old English sittan meant to sit, and also to remain in a place attending to something.
items.cn: 古英语 sittan 意为「坐」，也指留在某处照料某事。

items.en: Baby became the ordinary word for a very young child, replacing older native forms.
items.cn: baby 成为指幼儿的常用词，取代了更早的本族形式。

items.en: Baby-sitter is recorded in the 1930s for a person paid to sit with a child.
items.cn: baby-sitter 于 1930 年代有记载，指受雇陪看孩子的人。

items.en: The verb babysit was formed backwards from the noun in the 1940s.
items.cn: 动词 babysit 于 1940 年代由名词反向构出。

items.en: Later in the century the verb spread to machines, projects and fragile processes.
items.cn: 该世纪后期这个动词扩展到机器、项目与易出问题的流程。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the sit compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for minding a person or a thing.
note.cn: 形近组保留 sit 复合词；近义组列出其他表示照看人或物的词。

entries.definition: A person paid to mind a child.
To live in a house while owners are away.
To rest on the seat of the body.
One who sits, or poses for a portrait.
To look after for a time.
To care for children as a job.
To watch over work or people.

normalIntro.en: Babysit is baby plus sit, built backwards from babysitter: sit by the baby until the parents return.
normalIntro.cn: babysit 是 baby 加 sit，由 babysitter 反向构出：坐在婴儿旁边直到父母回来。

normal.en: The past form is babysat, not babysitted.
normal.cn: 过去式是 babysat，不是 babysitted。

normal.en: Babysit for someone, babysit someone directly.
normal.cn: 既可接 for 加人，也可直接接人。

normal.en: The job noun is babysitting.
normal.cn: 工作名词是 babysitting。

normal.en: Housesit follows the same pattern.
normal.cn: housesit 遵循同一构词方式。

normal.en: It extends to servers and projects.
normal.cn: 它可引申用于服务器与项目。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled beside a cot.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子拉到婴儿床边。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp left on until a key turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯亮着直到钥匙转动。

abstract.en: Think of a machine you dare not leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一台你不敢离开的机器。

examples.en: Can you babysit on Friday evening?
examples.cn: 你周五晚上能来看孩子吗？

examples.en: She babysat for three families that year.
examples.cn: 那一年她替三户人家看孩子。

examples.en: He had to babysit the printer all morning.
examples.cn: 他整个上午都得盯着那台打印机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：baby「婴儿」+ sit「坐」——坐在婴儿旁边守着，就是 babysit；过去式跟着 sit 变成 babysat。

root: baby 为育儿用语，sit 出自古英语 sittan「坐、留守」；1930 年代先有 babysitter「陪看孩子的人」，1940 年代反向构出动词 babysit。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same patient sitting: beside a cot until the parents come home, and beside a fragile task until it is safe.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一种耐心守坐：守在婴儿床边直到父母回家，守在易出问题的任务旁直到它稳妥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hours kept beside a cot after the parents go out
core.cn: 核心意象：父母出门后守在摇篮边的那几个小时

branches.en: A Saturday night for the neighbours.
Twice a week for a sister.
branches.cn: 每周两次替姐姐看孩子。
整个上午盯着的打印机。

branches.en: Both refuse to leave the thing alone.
branches.cn: 两者都不肯把对象放着不管。

intro.en: Babysit is baby plus sit; the same compound pattern gives housesit and petsit, and -er turns it back into babysitter.
intro.cn: babysit 是 baby 加 sit；同一复合方式产生 housesit 与 petsit，而 -er 又把它变回 babysitter。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native rather than Latin; Latin sedere, to sit, gives session and sedentary beside the English sit.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语而非拉丁语；旁边的拉丁语 sedere「坐」产生 session 与 sedentary。

definition_zh: n. 未婚男子；单身汉；学士（学位）；（旧时）年轻骑士
definition_en: An unmarried man; a first university degree; historically, a young knight without a following.
core_image: 一个人吃饭一个人住的那张桌子
scene: 他四十岁仍是单身，桌上摊着学士学位证书。He was still a bachelor at forty, his degree certificate spread on the table.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bachelor 指从未结婚的成年男子。

pos.zh: 未婚男子；学士；年轻骑士

senses.title: An unmarried man
senses.definition: a man who has never married, especially one living alone
senses.definitionCN: 从未结婚的男子，尤指独居者
senses.example: He lived as a bachelor for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他过了三十年单身生活。
senses.why: The word named a young man without land or a household of his own, so the unmarried sense came first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指没有土地也没有自己家室的年轻人，因此未婚义最先出现。

senses.title: A first university degree
senses.definition: the first degree awarded by a university, below a master and a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予的第一级学位，低于硕士与博士
senses.example: She holds a bachelor of science in biology.
senses.exampleCN: 她持有生物学理学士学位。
senses.why: Universities borrowed the knightly rank for their lowest grade, so a student became a bachelor before a master.
senses.whyCN: 大学把骑士等级借用为最低学阶，于是学生先成 bachelor 再成 master。

senses.title: A young knight
senses.definition: in medieval use, a knight too young or too poor to lead his own followers
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪用法中，指太年轻或太穷而无法自带随从的骑士
senses.example: The knight bachelor rode without a banner.
senses.exampleCN: 那位下级骑士出行不带旗号。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, and it explains the other two: a man not yet head of anything.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也解释了另外两个：一个尚未成为任何事物之首的男人。

intro.en: Bachelor comes from Old French bacheler, a young man or aspirant knight, from Medieval Latin baccalaris, whose origin is uncertain but may mean a farm hand.
intro.cn: bachelor 来自古法语 bacheler「年轻人、见习骑士」，出自中世纪拉丁语 baccalaris，其来源不确定，可能意为「农庄雇工」。

items.en: Baccalaris named a young man of low rank, possibly a worker on a farm estate.
items.cn: baccalaris 指地位较低的年轻人，可能是农庄上的雇工。

items.en: Old French bacheler meant a young man training to be a knight.
items.cn: 古法语 bacheler 意为「受训成为骑士的年轻人」。

items.en: Middle English took the word for a young knight without his own banner.
items.cn: 中古英语借入该词，指没有自己旗号的下级骑士。

items.en: Universities used it for the first degree, below master and doctor.
items.cn: 大学用它指第一级学位，低于硕士与博士。

items.en: The same century fixed the sense of a man who has never married.
items.cn: 同一个世纪确立了「从未结婚的男子」这一义项。

items.en: The spelling settled as bachelor, while baccalaureate kept a learned Latin look.
items.cn: 拼法定为 bachelor，而 baccalaureate 保留了学术味的拉丁外观。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the degree family; the near-meaning group lists words for people who are not married.
note.cn: 形近组保留学位词族；近义组列出表示未婚者的词。

entries.definition: A first degree or school-leaving exam.
entries.definitionCN: 学士学位或中学毕业会考。

entries.definition: A head of state or university.
Not married or in a relationship.
An unmarried woman, in older use.
A person who holds a degree.

normalIntro.en: Bachelor began as a young knight with no followers, so it came to mean a man with no household and then the lowest degree.
normalIntro.cn: bachelor 起初指没有随从的年轻骑士，于是转指没有家室的男子，再指最低一级学位。

normal.en: The degree phrase takes an apostrophe s.
normal.cn: 学位短语要加撇号 s。

normal.en: Bachelor of Arts and of Science are the pair.
normal.cn: 文学学士与理学士是一对。

normal.en: A confirmed bachelor will not marry.
normal.cn: 铁心单身汉指不打算结婚的人。

normal.en: Bachelorhood is the state, bachelor the man.
normal.cn: bachelorhood 是状态，bachelor 是人。

normal.en: Knight bachelor is the old rank.
normal.cn: knight bachelor 是旧时等级。

abstract.en: Picture a table laid for one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只摆一人份的餐桌。

abstract.en: Imagine a rider with no banner behind him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名身后无旗的骑手。

abstract.en: Think of the first rung of a ladder.
abstract.cn: 想象梯子的第一级。

examples.en: He remained a bachelor all his life.
examples.cn: 他一生未婚。

examples.en: She finished her bachelor of engineering.
examples.cn: 她读完了工学学士。

examples.en: They rented a small bachelor flat.
examples.cn: 他们租了一间小的单身公寓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「拜了个了」——把婚事拜别了结，一个人过，就是 bachelor 单身汉；学位义则是学阶里的「第一级」。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 baccalaris「低位年轻人」经古法语 bacheler「见习骑士」入英语；因指「尚未成家立业者」，衍生出未婚男子与大学第一级学位两义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses describe a man not yet head of anything: no banner, no household, and no higher degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在描述一个尚未成为任何事物之首的男人：没有旗号、没有家室、没有更高学位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table laid for one person only
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人吃饭一个人住的那张桌子

branches.en: A man of forty living alone.
A knight riding without a banner.
Both name a man without a following.
branches.cn: 两者都指没有随从的人。

intro.en: Bachelor is a single French root with the agent ending -or; -ette marks the female form and -hood the state.
intro.cn: bachelor 是一个法语词根加施事词尾 -or；-ette 标记女性形式，-hood 标记状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is baccalaris, a young man of low rank; Latin bacca, berry, was later imagined inside baccalaureate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 baccalaris「低位年轻人」；后来人们又把拉丁语 bacca「浆果」附会进 baccalaureate。

definition_zh: n. 杆菌；芽孢杆菌；（大写）芽孢杆菌属
definition_en: A rod-shaped bacterium; with a capital, a genus of such bacteria that form resistant spores.
core_image: 显微镜下一根根短棒似的小东西
scene: 培养皿里那株杆菌一夜之间铺满了培养基。The bacillus in the dish had covered the medium overnight.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bacillus 泛指呈杆状的细菌，复数为 bacilli。

senses.title: Any rod-shaped bacterium
senses.definition: a bacterium whose cell is shaped like a short rod, whatever its species
senses.definitionCN: 细胞形如短棒的细菌，不论其种类
senses.example: The smear showed a few bacilli.
senses.exampleCN: 涂片显示有少量杆菌。
senses.why: Bacillus is Latin for a little rod, so the name describes the shape seen under the lens, not the disease.
senses.whyCN: bacillus 在拉丁语中意为「小棒」，因此这个名字描述镜下所见的形状，而非疾病。

senses.title: The spore-forming genus
senses.definition: with a capital, a genus of rod-shaped bacteria that form spores able to survive heat and drying
senses.definitionCN: 大写时指一个杆状细菌属，能形成耐热耐干的孢子
senses.example: Bacillus spores survive boiling for minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 芽孢杆菌的孢子能在沸水中存活数分钟。
senses.why: Once microbiology needed exact genera, the shape word was fixed as a formal name for one group.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学需要精确的属名之后，这个形状词就被定为某一群的正式名称。

intro.en: Bacillus is Late Latin bacillus, a little rod, a diminutive of Latin baculus, a stick or staff; the plural bacilli keeps the Latin pattern.
intro.cn: bacillus 是晚期拉丁语 bacillus「小棒」，为拉丁语 baculus「棍、杖」的指小形式；复数 bacilli 保留拉丁语变化。

items.en: A root meaning a staff or support stands behind words for sticks and props.
items.cn: 一个表示「杖、支撑」的词根支撑着棍棒与支柱类的词。

items.en: Latin baculus meant a stick or walking staff, the plain word for a rod.
items.cn: 拉丁语 baculus 意为「棍、手杖」，是指杆的普通词。

items.en: The diminutive bacillus meant a little rod, used for small slender objects.
items.cn: 指小形式 bacillus 意为「小棒」，用于细长的物件。

items.en: Naturalists used bacillus for rod-shaped organisms seen under early microscopes.
items.cn: 博物学者用 bacillus 指早期显微镜下所见的杆状生物。

items.en: Bacteriology fixed Bacillus as a genus of spore-forming rods in the 1870s.
items.cn: 细菌学在 1870 年代把 Bacillus 定为产芽孢杆菌的一个属。

items.en: English kept the Latin plural bacilli, and the word entered public health writing.
items.cn: 英语保留拉丁语复数 bacilli，这个词也进入公共卫生文献。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bacterium family; the near-meaning group lists other shape names used for bacteria.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bacterium 词族；近义组列出用于细菌的其他形状名称。

normalIntro.en: Bacillus is Latin for a little rod, from baculus, a staff: the name is the shape you see in the lens.
normalIntro.cn: bacillus 在拉丁语中意为「小棒」，出自 baculus「杖」：这个名字就是你在镜头里看到的形状。

normal.en: One bacillus, many bacilli.
normal.cn: 单数 bacillus，复数 bacilli。

normal.en: Bacterium and bacteria follow the same rule.
normal.cn: bacterium 与 bacteria 遵循同一规则。

normal.en: A capital Bacillus means the genus.
normal.cn: 大写 Bacillus 指那个属。

normal.en: The tubercle bacillus causes tuberculosis.
normal.cn: 结核杆菌引起结核病。

normal.en: Coccus is round, bacillus is rod-shaped.
normal.cn: coccus 是球形，bacillus 是杆状。

abstract.en: Picture matchsticks scattered on glass.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃片上散落的火柴棍。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny staff under a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象镜头下一根微小的杖。

abstract.en: Think of a seed that survives boiling.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗经得起煮沸的种子。

examples.en: The bacillus was identified within a day.
examples.cn: 那株杆菌一天内就被鉴定出来。

examples.en: Several bacilli appeared in the sample.
examples.cn: 样本中出现了若干杆菌。

examples.en: Heat does not always kill bacillus spores.
examples.cn: 加热并不总能杀死杆菌孢子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：bacul「棍、杖」+ -illus「小」——一根根小棍子，就是 bacillus 杆菌；复数按拉丁语变 bacilli。

root: 拉丁语 baculus「棍、杖」的指小形式 bacillus「小棒」被博物学借来指镜下杆状生物；1870 年代大写 Bacillus 定为产芽孢杆菌属。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same little rod: any bacterium of that shape, and the one genus formally named after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一根「小棒」：任何呈该形状的细菌，以及以之正式命名的那个属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: short rods scattered under the microscope glass
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下一根根短棒似的小东西

branches.en: A few rods seen in a smear.
branches.cn: 涂片中见到的少量杆菌。

branches.en: Both are named for the rod shape.

intro.en: Bacillus is bacul plus the Latin diminutive -illus; the same shrinking endings give -ule and -cule in other scientific words.
intro.cn: bacillus 是 bacul 加拉丁语指小后缀 -illus；同样的缩小词尾在其他科学词中表现为 -ule 与 -cule。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is baculus, a staff, and bacillus, a little rod; Greek bakterion, a small staff, gives bacterium beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 baculus「杖」与 bacillus「小棒」；旁边的希腊语 bakterion「小棍」产生 bacterium。

definition_zh: n. 背痛；腰痛（通常为持续性钝痛）
definition_en: A pain in the back, usually a dull and lasting one.
core_image: 直不起腰时后背那条隐隐的痛线
scene: 搬了一整天箱子，他晚上直不起腰。Lifting boxes all day left him with a bad backache by evening.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：backache 指背部的疼痛，常作不可数名词。

senses.title: Pain in the back
senses.definition: a dull lasting pain anywhere along the back, treated as an uncountable condition
senses.definitionCN: 背部任何位置的持续钝痛，作不可数的身体状况看待
senses.example: She has had backache since the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 她自从那次跌倒后一直背痛。
senses.why: Backache joins back with ache, an old word for continuing pain, so it names a state rather than a sharp blow.
senses.whyCN: backache 由 back 与 ache 组成，ache 是指持续疼痛的旧词，因此它指一种状态而非一次剧痛。

senses.title: A bout of that pain
senses.definition: countably, one spell of such pain, as when a person speaks of recurrent aches
senses.definitionCN: 作可数用法时指一次这样的疼痛发作，如谈到反复发作的疼痛
senses.example: He gets backaches after long drives.
senses.exampleCN: 长途开车后他就会背痛发作。
senses.why: Because the condition returns in spells, speakers began counting the spells, giving the plural.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种状况会一阵阵回来，使用者开始数这些发作，于是有了复数。

intro.en: Backache is back plus ache; back is Old English baec, and ache comes from Old English acan, to ache, a native verb long confused in spelling with the noun.
intro.cn: backache 是 back 加 ache；back 是古英语 baec，ache 出自古英语 acan「疼痛」，这个本族动词的拼写长期与名词相混。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back of a body, the native word still in use.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「身体的背部」，是沿用至今的本族词。

items.en: Old English acan was a verb meaning to give continuing pain.
items.cn: 古英语 acan 是动词，意为「持续作痛」。

items.en: Middle English had the verb ake and the noun ache, with different sounds.
items.cn: 中古英语有动词 ake 与名词 ache，读音不同。

items.en: Dr Johnson fixed the spelling ache for both, following the noun form.
items.cn: 约翰逊博士按名词形式把两者的拼写定为 ache。

items.en: Backache is recorded in the nineteenth century as complaints of work posture grew.
items.cn: 随着劳作姿势引起的病症增多，backache 于十九世纪有记载。

items.en: Today it appears in occupational health as lower back pain of mechanical origin.
items.cn: 今天它出现在职业健康领域，指力学原因引起的下背痛。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ache compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for pain in the trunk of the body.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ache 复合词；近义组列出表示躯干疼痛的其他词。

entries.definition: The spine, or firmness of will.

normalIntro.en: Backache is back plus ache: a continuing dull pain along the back, and the plural counts its spells.
normalIntro.cn: backache 是 back 加 ache：沿背部的持续钝痛，复数则数它一次次发作。

normal.en: Usually uncountable: have backache.
normal.cn: 通常不可数：have backache。

normal.en: The plural counts separate spells.
normal.cn: 复数指一次次单独的发作。

normal.en: Lower backache is the commonest kind.
normal.cn: 下背痛是最常见的一种。

normal.en: Ache is dull; pain can be sharp.
normal.cn: ache 是钝痛，pain 可以是剧痛。

normal.en: Toothache and headache follow the pattern.
normal.cn: toothache 与 headache 遵循同一构词。

abstract.en: Picture a line of dull heat along the spine.
abstract.cn: 想象沿脊柱的一条闷热之线。

abstract.en: Imagine standing up only halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象只能直起一半的腰。

abstract.en: Think of a chair that never quite helps.
abstract.cn: 想象一把怎么坐都不解决问题的椅子。

examples.en: Backache kept her from the garden.
examples.cn: 背痛让她没法去花园。

examples.en: A firm mattress eased his backache.
examples.cn: 硬一点的床垫缓解了他的背痛。

examples.en: Repeated backaches forced him to stop lifting.
examples.cn: 反复的背痛发作迫使他不再搬重物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「背」+ ache「持续作痛」——背上那条不断的钝痛，就是 backache；同法还有 toothache、headache。

root: 古英语 baec「背」与 acan「持续作痛」合成 backache；ache 的拼写在十八世纪按名词形式统一，十九世纪该复合词随劳作病症增多而通行。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same dull line of pain: the lasting condition, and one spell of it counted separately.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条钝痛之线：持续的状况，以及被单独计数的一次发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dull line of pain along the back when you cannot stand straight
core.cn: 核心意象：直不起腰时后背那条隐隐的痛线

branches.en: A back sore after lifting boxes.
Spells brought on by long drives.
Repeated bouts that stop the lifting.
branches.cn: 反复到让人不再搬重物的发作。
同一状况，可计数或不计数。

intro.en: Backache is back plus ache; the same ache ending builds toothache and headache, while -breaking gives backbreaking.
intro.cn: backache 是 back 加 ache；同一 ache 词尾构成 toothache 与 headache，而 -breaking 则给出 backbreaking。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native; Latin lumbus, loin, gives lumbago and lumbar, and dolor, pain, gives dolorous beside them.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语；拉丁语 lumbus「腰」产生 lumbago 与 lumbar，dolor「痛」则产生 dolorous。

definition_zh: n. 脊柱；脊椎；骨干；支柱；骨气；坚毅
definition_en: The spine; the main support or strongest part of a system; firmness of character.
core_image: 撑起整个身子的那一串骨头
scene: 她是整个项目的骨干，谁的活卡住都找她。She was the backbone of the project, and everyone came to her when work stalled.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：backbone 比喻一个组织或系统中起支撑作用的核心部分。

senses.title: The row of back bones
senses.definition: the line of joined bones running down the back, which holds the body upright
senses.definitionCN: 沿背部相连的一列骨头，支撑身体直立
senses.example: He injured his backbone in the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在跌倒中伤到了脊柱。
senses.why: Backbone is back plus bone, naming the structure by where it sits and what it is made of.
senses.whyCN: backbone 由 back 与 bone 组成，用位置与材质来命名这个结构。

senses.title: The main support
senses.definition: the part of a system, group or network on which everything else depends
senses.definitionCN: 系统、群体或网络中其余部分都依赖的那一部分
senses.example: Small farms are the backbone of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 小农场是该地区的支柱。
senses.why: Because the spine holds the whole body, the word moved to whatever holds a whole organisation together.
senses.whyCN: 因为脊柱撑起整个身体，这个词便转指任何把整个组织撑起来的东西。

senses.title: Firmness of character
senses.definition: the courage to hold a position under pressure, thought of as an inner spine
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下坚持立场的勇气，被看作内在的脊梁
senses.example: It takes backbone to admit a mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 承认错误需要骨气。
senses.why: A body without a spine collapses, so a person without firmness was described as having no backbone.
senses.whyCN: 没有脊柱的身体会塌下去，因此没有坚定立场的人就被说成没有 backbone。

intro.en: Backbone is back plus bone, both native English words; the anatomical sense is medieval, and the figurative senses of support and courage follow from it.
intro.cn: backbone 是 back 加 bone，两者都是英语本族词；解剖义见于中世纪，「支柱」与「骨气」的比喻义由此衍生。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back of a body, the surface opposite the chest.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「身体的背部」，即与胸相对的那一面。

items.en: Old English ban meant a bone, and also the hard inner part of anything.
items.cn: 古英语 ban 意为「骨」，也指任何事物的坚硬内核。

items.en: Middle English backbon named the spine as the bone of the back.
items.cn: 中古英语 backbon 用「背之骨」来指脊柱。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word named the chief support of a structure or group.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，这个词指某结构或群体的主要支撑。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it came to mean firmness of will, often in the negative.
items.cn: 十九世纪它转指意志的坚定，常用于否定表述。

items.en: Computing borrowed it for the main line that carries traffic between smaller networks.
items.cn: 计算机领域借它指在较小网络之间承载流量的主干线路。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the back compounds; the near-meaning group lists words for a spine, a support and a firm will.
note.cn: 形近组保留 back 复合词；近义组列出表示脊柱、支撑与坚定意志的词。

entries.definition: A dull pain in the back.
A stage cloth, or a setting.
A hard part of the skeleton.

normalIntro.en: Backbone is back plus bone: the spine that holds you up, then anything that holds a system or a will up.
normalIntro.cn: backbone 是 back 加 bone：撑起你的脊柱，进而指撑起某个系统或某种意志的东西。

normal.en: The backbone of something is the set phrase.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 the backbone of 某事物。

normal.en: Spine is the medical word, backbone the plain one.
normal.cn: spine 是医学用词，backbone 更平易。

normal.en: No backbone means no firmness.
normal.cn: 没有 backbone 就是没有骨气。

normal.en: Networks use it for the main line.
normal.cn: 网络领域用它指主干线路。

normal.en: The plural backbones is rare but regular.
normal.cn: 复数 backbones 少见但规则。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of blocks holding a body tall.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞骨块把身体撑高。

abstract.en: Imagine one beam carrying a whole roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一根梁撑起整个屋顶。

abstract.en: Think of a person who will not bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不肯弯下的人。

examples.en: The scan showed a healthy backbone.
examples.cn: 扫描显示脊柱健康。

examples.en: Rail is the backbone of freight here.
examples.cn: 铁路是这里货运的支柱。

examples.en: She showed real backbone in the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上表现出真正的骨气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「背」+ bone「骨」——背上的那串骨头就是脊柱；撑起组织的是骨干，撑起人的是骨气。

root: 古英语 baec「背」与 ban「骨」合成中古英语 backbon「脊柱」；因脊柱撑起全身，十六世纪衍生「支柱」义，十九世纪再衍生「骨气」义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are the same holding-up: bones holding a body, a core holding a system, and will holding a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是同一种「撑起」：骨头撑起身体，核心撑起系统，意志撑起一个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the string of bones that holds the whole body up
core.cn: 核心意象：撑起整个身子的那一串骨头

branches.en: A spine injured in a fall.
A person the whole project leans on.
Rail carrying the freight of a region.
A will that refuses to bend.

intro.en: Backbone is back plus bone; the same back element builds backdrop and backpack, while -y turns bone into bony.
intro.cn: backbone 是 back 加 bone；同一 back 成分构成 backdrop 与 backpack，而 -y 把 bone 变成 bony。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native; Latin spina, thorn, gives spine and spinal, and Latin columna gives column and pillar beside them.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语；拉丁语 spina「刺」产生 spine 与 spinal，columna 则产生 column，旁边还有 pillar。

definition_zh: n. （舞台后方的）背景幕；背景；（事件发生的）背景形势
definition_en: A painted cloth hung at the back of a stage; the general setting or conditions in which something happens.
core_image: 舞台最后面那块画着远山的布
scene: 谈判在通胀高企的背景下重启。The talks resumed against a backdrop of high inflation.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：backdrop 比喻事件发生时所处的整体形势或环境。

senses.title: The cloth behind the stage
senses.definition: a large painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage to show the scene of the action
senses.definitionCN: 挂在舞台后部的大块彩绘布，用来显示剧情场景
senses.example: The backdrop showed a harbour at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 背景幕上画着黄昏的港口。
senses.why: Backdrop is back plus drop, a theatre word for a cloth let down from above, so it names what hangs behind.
senses.whyCN: backdrop 是 back 加 drop——drop 是剧场用语，指从上方垂下的布，因此它指挂在后面的那块。

senses.title: The setting of an event
senses.definition: the conditions or surroundings against which an event is seen and understood
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件被观看与理解时所处的条件或环境
senses.example: The reforms came against a backdrop of unrest.
senses.exampleCN: 改革是在动荡的背景下推出的。
senses.why: Once the stage picture was familiar, the word moved to the situation that stands behind any public event.
senses.whyCN: 舞台画面为人熟知之后，这个词便转指任何公共事件背后的形势。

intro.en: Backdrop is back plus drop, where drop is a theatre term for a curtain let down from the flies; the compound is recorded in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: backdrop 是 back 加 drop——drop 是剧场术语，指从吊景区垂下的幕；这个复合词于二十世纪初有记载。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back, the side away from the viewer.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「后面」，即背离观看者的一侧。

items.en: Old English dropa meant a drop of liquid, from the verb to fall in drops.
items.cn: 古英语 dropa 意为「一滴液体」，出自表示滴落的动词。

items.en: By the eighteenth century drop named a curtain lowered onto the stage.
items.cn: 到十八世纪 drop 指垂放到舞台上的幕布。

items.en: The compound backdrop is recorded in the 1910s for the rear painted cloth.
items.cn: 复合词 backdrop 于 1910 年代有记载，指后方的彩绘幕布。

items.en: Journalism soon used it for the conditions behind an event.
items.cn: 新闻界很快用它指事件背后的形势条件。

items.en: The phrase against a backdrop of became a standard opening in reporting.
items.cn: 「在……背景下」这一短语成为报道的标准开头之一。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the back compounds and the theatre word drop; the near-meaning group lists words for a setting.
note.cn: 形近组保留 back 复合词与剧场词 drop；近义组列出表示背景环境的词。

entries.definition: The setting, or a person’s history.
A small bead of liquid, or a fall.
A bag carried on the back.
The painted structures on a stage.
The social environment of a person.

normalIntro.en: Backdrop is back plus drop, a theatre curtain let down behind the actors: then any situation standing behind an event.
normalIntro.cn: backdrop 是 back 加 drop——垂在演员身后的剧场幕布；进而指站在事件背后的任何形势。

normal.en: The set phrase is against a backdrop of.
normal.cn: 固定短语是 against a backdrop of。

normal.en: Background is wider; backdrop is more visual.
normal.cn: background 更宽泛，backdrop 更有画面感。

normal.en: A drop is a hanging stage cloth.
normal.cn: drop 指垂挂的舞台幕布。

normal.en: It is countable: two backdrops.
normal.cn: 它可数：two backdrops。

normal.en: Scenery is built, a backdrop is hung.
normal.cn: scenery 是搭建的，backdrop 是垂挂的。

abstract.en: Picture distant hills painted on cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象布上画着的远山。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole city behind one speech.
abstract.cn: 想象一场演讲背后的整座城市。

abstract.en: Think of a frame that makes the figure readable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个让人物得以被读懂的画框。

examples.en: They rolled up the old backdrop.
examples.cn: 他们把旧背景幕卷了起来。

examples.en: The strike happened against a backdrop of cuts.
examples.cn: 罢工发生在削减开支的背景下。

examples.en: Snow peaks formed a dramatic backdrop.
examples.cn: 雪峰构成了引人注目的背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「后面」+ drop「垂下的幕布」——垂在舞台最后面的那块布就是 backdrop；引申为事件的背景形势。

root: 古英语 baec「后」与 dropa「滴」合成的剧场词 drop「垂幕」，在 1910 年代组成 backdrop「背景幕」；1930 年代新闻界引申为事件背景。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are what hangs behind: a painted cloth behind the actors, and a situation behind the news.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是「挂在后面的东西」：演员身后的彩绘幕布，以及新闻背后的形势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth of painted far hills at the very back of the stage
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台最后面那块画着远山的布

branches.cn: 在高物价中举行的谈判。
以削减开支为背景的罢工。

branches.en: Both stand behind what is watched.
branches.cn: 两者都立于被观看之物的后方。

intro.en: Backdrop is back plus drop; the same back element builds background and backbone, while -ground gives the wider cousin.
intro.cn: backdrop 是 back 加 drop；同一 back 成分构成 background 与 backbone，而 -ground 则给出更宽泛的近亲。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native; Latin contexere, to weave together, gives context, and Latin scaena gives scene and scenery.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语；拉丁语 contexere「编织在一起」产生 context，scaena 则产生 scene 与 scenery。

definition_zh: 背景；出身；幕后
definition_en: the area behind the main subject, or a person's past experience
core_image: 舞台后面一块素色幕布，演员站在幕布前
scene: 画家把最后一个人物放进画面。The mountains form a quiet background.
sceneCN: 这里 background 是「背景」（第 1 个义项：画面中主体后面的部分）；句意是群山构成了一片安静的背景。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「后部」，background 由其与 ground 复合而成
由 background 加 -er 构成，义为「背景简报」

senses.title: The area behind
senses.definition: the area or scenery behind the main object
senses.definitionCN: 主体后面的区域或景物
senses.example: The mountains form a quiet background.
senses.exampleCN: 群山构成了一片安静的背景。
senses.why: Background is simply back plus ground, the ground at the back of a picture, so its first sense is spatial.
senses.whyCN: background 就是 back 加 ground，即画的后方那片地，所以第一个义项是空间性的。

senses.title: Past experience
senses.definition: the family, education and experience that shaped a person
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一个人的家庭、教育与经历
senses.example: Her background in science helped the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的科学背景帮了团队。
senses.why: The ground behind a figure is not seen in detail but supports it, just as a person's past supports what they do now.
senses.whyCN: 人物背后的那片地看不真切，却托着人物，正如一个人的过去托着他现在做的事。

senses.title: Behind the main activity
senses.definition: the less visible part of a situation or activity
senses.definitionCN: 情况或活动中不太显眼的部分
senses.example: Several helpers worked in the background.
senses.exampleCN: 几位助手在幕后工作。
senses.why: If the background is what lies behind the subject, then people who work out of sight are working in the background.
senses.whyCN: 如果背景是主体后面的东西，那么看不见的人在做事，就是在幕后工作。

intro.en: Background is a compound of two plain English words.
intro.cn: background 是两个朴素的英语词复合而成。

items.en: bæc meant 'the back'.
items.cn: bæc 意为「背部」。

items.en: grund meant 'the ground'.
items.cn: grund 意为「地面」。

items.en: the compound named the ground behind a painted figure.
items.cn: 复合词指画中人物后面的地。

items.en: It extended to a person's past.
items.cn: 它扩展到指一个人的过去。

items.en: It also names the unseen part of activity.
items.cn: 如今也指活动中看不见的部分。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in ground; the near-meaning group gives setting and history words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 ground 结尾；近义组是表示环境与经历的词。

entries.definition: beneath the surface of the earth

normalIntro.en: Background is literally the ground at the back of the picture.
normalIntro.cn: background 字面上就是画面后方的那片地。

normal.en: In the background means not in the main view.
normal.cn: in the background 意为不在主要视野里。

normal.en: Family background names where a person comes from.
normal.cn: family background 指一个人的家庭出身。

normal.en: Background music is music under the main sound.
normal.cn: background music 是衬在主要声音下的音乐。

normal.en: The plural is backgrounds.
normal.cn: 复数是 backgrounds。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: BACK-ground.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a plain cloth behind a figure on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台人物身后的一块素幕。

abstract.en: See a photo where only the near faces are sharp.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只有近处人脸清晰的照片。

abstract.en: See a row of helpers moving in the dim light.
abstract.cn: 想象一排助手在暗光里忙碌。

examples.en: The mountains form a quiet background.
examples.cn: 群山构成了一片安静的背景。

examples.en: Her background in science helped the team.
examples.cn: 她的科学背景帮了团队。

examples.en: Several helpers worked in the background.
examples.cn: 几位助手在幕后工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: back（后面）加 ground（地面）：画面后面那片地就是背景，人的过去也像这片地。

root: 由 back「后面」与 ground「地面」复合而成，十六世纪起用于绘画，指人物后面的那片地；后引申为个人经历与幕后的部分。

sensesIntro.en: The ground behind a figure, a person's past and unseen work are one spatial idea stretched in time.
sensesIntro.cn: 人物身后的地、个人的过去与看不见的工作，是同一个空间想法在时间上的延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain cloth behind a figure on stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台人物身后的一块素幕。

intro.en: The ground root, 'earth', also gives playground, underground and groundwork.
intro.cn: 词根 ground 意为「土地」，也构成 playground、underground 与 groundwork。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; both parts are English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，两个组成部分都是英语本族词。

items.meaning: a painted cloth at the back

definition_zh: n. 双肩背包；背包；v. 背着背包旅行；徒步自助旅行
definition_en: A bag carried on the back by two shoulder straps; as a verb, to travel cheaply carrying such a bag.
core_image: 两条肩带把全部家当挂在背上
scene: 他把两天的衣物塞进背包就出门了。He stuffed two days of clothes into his backpack and left.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：backpack 指用两条肩带背在背上的包。

senses.title: A bag worn on the back
senses.definition: a bag with two shoulder straps, carried on the back to leave the hands free
senses.definitionCN: 带两条肩带、背在背上以腾出双手的包
senses.example: Her backpack held a tent and a stove.
senses.exampleCN: 她的背包里装着一顶帐篷和一个炉子。
senses.why: Backpack is back plus pack, so it names a load by where it is carried rather than by its shape.
senses.whyCN: backpack 是 back 加 pack，因此它用「背在哪里」而不是形状来命名这份负载。

senses.title: To travel with one
senses.definition: to travel cheaply and independently, carrying one’s belongings in such a bag
senses.definitionCN: 以背包携带行李，廉价而自主地旅行
senses.example: They backpacked across three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们背包走过三个国家。
senses.why: The bag came to stand for a whole style of travel, so the noun turned into a verb for that style.
senses.whyCN: 这种包代表了一整种旅行方式，于是名词转为表示该方式的动词。

intro.en: Backpack is back plus pack; pack came through Middle Dutch pakke, of uncertain origin, and the compound is recorded in American English in the 1910s.
intro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack；pack 经中古荷兰语 pakke 传入，来源不确定，这个复合词于 1910 年代在美式英语中有记载。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back, the surface that carries a load.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「背」，即承载负荷的那一面。

items.en: Middle Dutch pakke meant a bundle or bale, a word of trade rather than learning.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pakke 意为「捆、包」，是商贸用语而非学术词。

items.en: Middle English packe named a bundle carried by a person or an animal.
items.cn: 中古英语 packe 指由人或牲畜驮运的捆包。

items.en: American English formed backpack in the 1910s for a bag with shoulder straps.
items.cn: 美式英语在 1910 年代造出 backpack，指带肩带的包。

items.en: The verb meaning to travel with a backpack spread in the 1960s.
items.cn: 表示背包旅行的动词用法在 1960 年代流行开来。

items.en: The noun became standard for school bags and for hiking gear alike.
items.cn: 这个名词同时成为学生书包与徒步装备的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the pack family; the near-meaning group lists other bags and one word for the traveller.
note.cn: 形近组保留 pack 词族；近义组列出其他包袋与一个指旅行者的词。

entries.definition: A person who travels with a backpack.
A bundle, or to fill a bag.
To go back along a route.
A bag carried on the back.
A soldier’s or walker’s back bag.
A bag with a single long strap.

normalIntro.en: Backpack is back plus pack: a bundle carried on the back, and then the whole style of travel built around it.
normalIntro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack：背在背上的捆包，进而指围绕它形成的整种旅行方式。

normal.en: Two straps make it a backpack.
normal.cn: 两条肩带才叫 backpack。

normal.en: Rucksack is the British cousin.
normal.cn: rucksack 是英式的近亲。

normal.en: The verb gives backpacked and backpacking.
normal.cn: 动词有 backpacked 与 backpacking。

normal.en: The traveller is a backpacker.
normal.cn: 旅行者是 backpacker。

normal.en: Backpack through a place is the pattern.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 backpack through 某地。

abstract.en: Picture your whole week hanging on two straps.
abstract.cn: 想象一整周的家当挂在两条带子上。

abstract.en: Imagine hands free on a mountain path.
abstract.cn: 想象山路上双手空着。

abstract.en: Think of a hostel bed booked that morning.
abstract.cn: 想象当天早上才订的青年旅舍床位。

examples.en: He left his backpack on the train.
examples.cn: 他把背包落在火车上了。

examples.en: They backpacked for six weeks.
examples.cn: 他们背包旅行了六周。

examples.en: The backpack straps dug into her shoulders.
examples.cn: 背包肩带勒进她的肩膀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「背」+ pack「捆包」——背在背上的包就是 backpack；背上它去旅行，就是动词「背包游」。

root: 古英语 baec「背」加经中古荷兰语 pakke 传入的 pack「捆包」，1910 年代美式英语合成 backpack；1960 年代衍生动词「背包旅行」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one load on two straps: the bag itself, and the independent travel that the bag makes possible.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一份挂在两条带子上的负载：包本身，以及这种包使之可能的自主旅行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two shoulder straps holding everything you own on your back
core.cn: 核心意象：两条肩带把全部家当挂在背上

branches.en: Two days of clothes stuffed in.
A tent and a stove carried.
The bag defines the way of going.
branches.cn: 这只包定义了出行方式。

intro.en: Backpack is back plus pack; -er makes the traveller, -ing the activity, and -age gives package from the same pack.
intro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack；-er 造出旅行者，-ing 造出活动，而 -age 由同一 pack 给出 package。

latinIntro.en: Pack is a trade word from Dutch rather than Latin; Latin sarcina, a bundle, gives the learned sarcina of botany beside it.
latinIntro.cn: pack 是来自荷兰语的商贸词而非拉丁语；旁边的拉丁语 sarcina「捆包」给出植物学中的学术用词。

definition_zh: 后台（的）；幕后（的）；私下地
definition_en: in or toward the area behind the stage in a theater; also, privately or behind the scenes
core_image: 幕布之后的暗廊，演员候场时压低的交谈
scene: 锣声未响，台上只有工作人员。The actors waited backstage for their cue.
sceneCN: 这里 backstage 指「在后台」（第 1 个义项：舞台后部区域）；句意：演员们在后台等待上场提示。

derivatives.zh: 充满后台气息的（非正式，backstage + -y）
在台侧；台下（同构反义方位词）

senses.title: The area behind the stage
senses.definition: the rooms, wings, and passages behind a theater stage
senses.definitionCN: 剧场舞台后方的房间、侧翼与通道
senses.example: The dressing rooms lie backstage, past the props shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 化妆间在后台，过了道具架就是。
senses.why: The compound says it plainly: back of the stage.
senses.whyCN: 复合词直白：舞台之后。

senses.title: Being in that area
senses.definition: in or toward that area, as adverb
senses.definitionCN: 副词用法，指在或往该区域
senses.example: Fans with passes could go backstage after the show.
senses.exampleCN: 持证粉丝演出后可进后台。
senses.why: The place-word turns freely into a direction.
senses.whyCN: 场所词可自由转为方位副词。

senses.title: Behind the scenes of public life
senses.definition: of negotiations or maneuvering, done privately away from public view
senses.definitionCN: 指谈判、运作在公众视线之外私下进行
senses.example: A backstage deal settled the strike overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一场幕后交易一夜之间化解了罢工。
senses.why: The theater image covers any public performance, including politics.
senses.whyCN: 剧场意象可覆盖一切「表演」，包括政治。

senses.title: The hidden work of performance
senses.definition: the labor of crew, dressers, and stagehands unseen by the audience
senses.definitionCN: 观众看不到的舞台工作与演出劳动
senses.example: Backstage chaos made the smooth show possible.
senses.exampleCN: 后台的兵荒马乱成就了台前的行云流水。
senses.why: Every visible ease hides invisible effort; the word marks the border.
senses.whyCN: 台前每分从容都藏着幕后辛劳，这个词标出界线。

senses.title: The private world of performers
senses.definition: the gossip, friendships, and rivalries among performers
senses.definitionCN: 演员之间的私交、八卦与竞争
senses.example: Backstage talk said the two leads barely spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 圈内传闻说两位主演几乎不说话。
senses.why: The hidden area names the hidden society.
senses.whyCN: 以隐蔽之地指称隐秘的圈子。

senses.title: Access and privilege
senses.definition: the status of being allowed where the public is not, as a backstage pass
senses.definitionCN: 获准进入禁区的特权，如后台通行证
senses.example: A backstage pass was the best souvenir of the tour.
senses.exampleCN: 那张后台通行证是巡演最好的纪念。
senses.why: Where the public cannot go, a token proves you can.
senses.whyCN: 公众进不去的地方，一纸凭证证明你能。

senses.title: Anxiety before appearing
senses.definition: the nerves of waiting to go on, metonymically
senses.definitionCN: 借代用法，指等待上场时的紧张心情
senses.example: She fought her backstage jitters with slow breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 她用深呼吸压制候场的紧张。
senses.why: The place holds the fear, so the place names it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧栖身于那个地方，地方便代它命名。

senses.title: In sports and media, the off-camera zone
senses.definition: the area behind arenas or studios, parallel to the theater use
senses.definitionCN: 体育馆、演播室中与剧场后台对应的区域
senses.example: Interviews moved backstage after the weigh-in.
senses.exampleCN: 称重仪式后，采访移到了后台。
senses.why: Any stage, literal or broadcast, has a back.
senses.whyCN: 凡有台处，无论实体还是镜头，皆有幕后。

intro.en: Backstage is a straightforward English compound of back plus stage, both native words; the theater sense solidified in the nineteenth century as playhouses grew wings and dressing rooms.
intro.cn: backstage 是地道的英语复合词，由 back + stage 构成，二者皆为本族词；19 世纪剧院增设侧翼与化妆间后，剧场义定型。

items.en: baec meant the back or rear; the adverbial back was already common.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 指背部、后方，副词 back 已很常用。

items.en: stage comes through Old French estage from Latin staticum, a standing place.
items.cn: stage 经古法语 estage 出自拉丁语 staticum「立足之地」。

items.en: stage named the raised platform for playing by the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 到 15 世纪，stage 已指演出的高台。

items.en: Early compounds like stage-door and back-door set the pattern.
items.cn: stage-door、back-door 等早期复合词确立构词模式。

items.en: Backstage appeared as theaters built real backstage regions; the word is attested from about 1890.
items.cn: 19 世纪剧院出现真正的后台区域，backstage 一词约 1890 年见于记载。

items.en: The figurative political sense and the pass-token sense grew in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 20 世纪发展出「幕后政治」义与「通行证」义。

note.en: Group one gathers compound twins and a spelling pair; group two gathers hidden-and-public words.
note.cn: 第一组收复合词孪生与拼写对；第二组收隐显对举的词。

entries.definition: off to the sides or out of sight; the wing-neighbor of backstage.
entries.definitionCN: 台侧或观众看不见处；backstage 的侧邻。

entries.definition: a swimming style; same back, unrelated stage.
entries.definitionCN: 仰泳；同一个 back，与舞台无关。

entries.definition: secret betrayal; its backstage flavor is metaphor only.
entries.definitionCN: 暗中陷害；与 backstage 的联想纯属比喻。

entries.definition: the set phrase for hidden workings.
entries.definitionCN: 表幕后运作的固定短语。

entries.definition: not on view; also of remarks not meant for the audience.
entries.definitionCN: 不在台上；也指非面向观众的言论。

entries.definition: kept within an organization, not public.
on the stage, in public view.
entries.definitionCN: 在台上、当众；backstage 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: The word draws its own map: back of the stage.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词自带地图：舞台之后。

normal.en: back plus stage: the compound is transparent.
normal.cn: back + stage：复合词一目了然。

normal.en: backstage pass is the pop-culture phrase to memorize.
normal.cn: backstage pass 是流行文化必背短语。

normal.en: Pair it with onstage for instant contrast.
normal.cn: 与 onstage 成对记，对比立现。

senses.title: Of Bacteria as a Class
senses.titleCN: 细菌的：属于细菌这一整类
senses.definition: relating to bacteria as a group of living things
senses.definitionCN: 与细菌这一类生物有关的
senses.example: Bacterial cells are far smaller than the cells of animals and plants.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌细胞远小于动物和植物的细胞。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun bacterium into an adjective of relation, meaning 'having to do with bacteria'. The core picture is the rod-shaped single cell first seen under the microscope.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 bacterium 变成表示关联的形容词，意为「与细菌有关」；核心画面就是最早在显微镜下看到的杆状单细胞。

senses.title: Caused by Bacteria
senses.titleCN: 细菌引起的：病因来自细菌
senses.definition: caused by bacteria rather than by a virus or another agent
senses.definitionCN: 由细菌而非病毒或其他病原引起的
senses.example: The wound developed a bacterial infection after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，伤口出现了细菌感染。
senses.why: Once bacteria are known to cause disease, the adjective marks the cause. Here -al no longer means merely 'about'; it means 'produced by', and it contrasts directly with viral.
senses.whyCN: 当细菌被确认能致病之后，这个形容词就用来标出病因；此时 -al 已不只是「关于」，而是「由……引起的」，并与 viral 直接对立。

senses.title: Of the Bacterial Cell
senses.titleCN: 细菌细胞的：讲细胞结构
senses.definition: relating to the structure or the single cell of a bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 与细菌的细胞结构或单个细菌细胞有关的
senses.example: The bacterial cell wall differs from the wall of a plant cell.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌的细胞壁与植物细胞的细胞壁不同。
senses.why: A bacterium is a single cell without a nucleus. When biologists say bacterial cell, they mean that whole prokaryotic unit, so the adjective points to a level of organisation rather than to a disease.
senses.whyCN: 细菌是没有细胞核的单细胞生物；生物学家说细菌细胞时，指的是整个原核细胞单位，因此这个形容词指向的是组织层次，而不是疾病。

senses.title: Of Growth and Culture
senses.titleCN: 细菌生长的：培养与增殖
senses.definition: relating to the growth or cultivation of bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 与细菌的生长或培养有关的
senses.example: Bacterial growth slowed once the dish was moved to a cold room.
senses.exampleCN: 培养皿被移到冷室后，细菌生长变慢了。
senses.why: In the laboratory bacteria are grown as a population, and growth is measured as the increase of that population. Bacterial growth therefore names a process over time, not a shape or a cell.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，细菌是作为一个种群来培养的，生长量就是该种群的增加量；因此 bacterial growth 指的是随时间发生的过程，而不是形状或单个细胞。

senses.title: Of Drug Resistance
senses.titleCN: 细菌耐药性的：药物不再有效
senses.definition: relating to the ability of bacteria to survive antibiotics
senses.definitionCN: 与细菌在抗生素作用下仍能存活的能力有关的
senses.example: Bacterial resistance to the drug appeared within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌对该药物的耐药性在两年内就出现了。
senses.why: Resistance is a trait of the bacteria themselves, not of the patient. The adjective assigns the trait to the organism, which is why the phrase is bacterial resistance rather than patient resistance.
senses.whyCN: 耐药性是细菌自身的性状，而不是病人的性状；这个形容词把该性状归属于生物体，所以说细菌耐药性，而不说病人耐药性。

senses.title: Of the Resident Flora
senses.titleCN: 细菌群落的：共居于某处的菌群
senses.definition: relating to the community of bacteria living in a place
senses.definitionCN: 与某一部位或环境中共同生活的细菌群落有关的
senses.example: Diet changes the bacterial flora of the gut within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食在数周内就会改变肠道的细菌群落。
senses.why: Flora here is the old word for the resident community of a place. Bacterial flora names which members of that community are meant, as opposed to fungal or viral members.
senses.whyCN: flora 在这里是旧用法，指某处常住的生物群落；bacterial flora 用来指明该群落中是细菌的那一部分，以区别于真菌或病毒部分。

senses.title: Of Contamination
senses.titleCN: 细菌污染的：食品与环境中的菌
senses.definition: relating to contamination by bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 与细菌造成的污染有关的
senses.example: The inspection found bacterial contamination in the water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 检查发现供水系统存在细菌污染。
senses.why: Contamination is the entry of unwanted bacteria into a substance or a place. The adjective marks the source of the fault, so the phrase names what kind of pollution is being reported.
senses.whyCN: 污染是指不需要的细菌进入某物质或某场所；这个形容词标出问题的来源，因此该短语说明的是被报告的是哪一类污染。

senses.title: Of Plant Disease
senses.titleCN: 植物细菌性病害的：植物病理学用法
senses.definition: relating to diseases of plants caused by bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 与由细菌引起的植物病害有关的
senses.example: Bacterial wilt destroyed the tomato field in a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌性枯萎病在一个季节里毁掉了整片番茄田。
senses.why: Plant pathology borrowed the same adjective for diseases with a bacterial cause, such as wilt and spot. The cause-and-effect sense of S2 is carried over to a new host, the plant.
senses.whyCN: 植物病理学借用了同一个形容词来指由细菌引起的病害，如枯萎病和斑点病；第 2 个义项的因果含义被原样移用到新的宿主——植物身上。

intro.en: Bacterial is the adjective of bacterium, whose name records what the first observers actually saw: a small rod. The Greek word for a stick became a scientific term for a whole class of single cells, and the adjective followed.
intro.cn: bacterial 是 bacterium 的形容词，而 bacterium 这个名字记录了最早观察者真正看到的东西：一根小棍。希腊语里表示棍子的词，后来成了整类单细胞生物的科学术语，形容词也随之产生。

items.en: Greek baktron meant 'stick, rod, staff, cudgel'. Its diminutive baktērion, 'small staff', supplied the name because the first bacteria seen under a microscope were rod-shaped.
items.cn: 希腊语 baktron 意为「棍、杆、杖、短棒」；其指小形式 baktērion 意为「小棍」，因为最早在显微镜下看到的细菌正是杆状的，于是这个词被用来命名。

items.en: The Greek word is usually connected with a reconstructed root *bak- 'staff used for support, peg', said to lie behind Latin baculum 'rod, walking stick'. De Vaan notes that *b was very rare in Indo-European and that the Celtic forms show an unexplained geminate, so the root may be a loanword from an unidentified source. This is a reconstructed form, and the origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个希腊词通常与重构词根 *bak-「支撑用的棍、木钉」联系起来，并被认为也衍生出拉丁语 baculum「杆、手杖」。但 De Vaan 指出 *b 在印欧语中极罕见，凯尔特语形式还出现无法解释的叠辅音，因此该词根可能是来自不明语言的借词。这是重构形式，来源不确定。

items.en: In 1838 the German naturalist Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg introduced bacterium as a scientific word for the rod-shaped microbes he observed. The plural bacteria is recorded from 1847, and the singular bacterium from about 1848 as a back-formation from that plural. The exact first English citation of the adjective is not fixed, so only its century is safe to state.
items.cn: 1838 年，德国博物学家克里斯蒂安·戈特弗里德·埃伦贝格把 bacterium 引入为科学术语，用来指他观察到的杆状微生物。复数 bacteria 记录于 1847 年，单数 bacterium 约 1848 年由该复数逆构而成。该形容词在英语中的确切首见书证并无定论，因此只能稳妥地说它出现于十九世纪。

items.en: Bacteria is a classical plural, but English writers have often treated it as a singular mass noun. Scientific style keeps bacterium for one cell and bacteria for two or more, which is why the adjective bacterial avoids the number question altogether.
items.cn: bacteria 是古典复数，但英语作者常把它当作单数集合名词使用。科学写作仍坚持一个细胞用 bacterium、两个及以上用 bacteria；正因如此，形容词 bacterial 干脆回避了单复数问题。

items.en: Bacteriology and bacteriological were coined in the later nineteenth century, when the germ theory of disease turned bacteria into an object of systematic study. The exact dates of these formations are approximate, since different authors introduced them independently.
items.cn: bacteriology 与 bacteriological 产生于十九世纪后半叶，当时病菌学说使细菌成为系统研究的对象。这些派生词的确切年代只是约数，因为不同作者曾各自独立地创制它们。

items.en: Modern medicine pairs bacterial with viral as two competing causes of infection. The pair matters clinically because antibiotics act on bacteria and not on viruses, so the adjective decides the treatment.
items.cn: 现代医学把 bacterial 与 viral 作为两类相对的感染病因并列。这一对立在临床上很重要，因为抗生素作用于细菌而不作用于病毒，所以这个形容词直接决定治疗方案。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same bacterium stem but filling different grammatical slots. The second group holds words with related meanings, none of which is an exact synonym.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一个 bacterium 词干上、但占据不同语法位置的一组词；第二组是意义相近、但没有一个完全同义的词。

entries.definition: The adverb of bacterial, meaning 'by or with bacteria'. It is rare and mostly appears in technical prose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词 bacterial 的副词形式，意为「以细菌方式地、借细菌作用地」；用法罕见，多见于技术性文字。

entries.definition: The study of bacteria, not the adjective describing them. The ending -logy marks a field of study.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究细菌的学科，而不是描述细菌的形容词；词尾 -logy 表示一门学问。

entries.definition: Killing bacteria, as opposed to merely slowing their growth. The second element comes from Latin caedere 'to cut down'.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死细菌的，与仅仅抑制其生长不同；后半部分来自拉丁语 caedere「砍倒」。

entries.definition: Of microbes in general, including fungi and protists, not only bacteria. It is broader than bacterial and is the better choice when the group is mixed.
entries.definitionCN: 指微生物的，范围包括真菌与原生生物，而不只是细菌；比 bacterial 更宽，群体混杂时更宜用这个词。

entries.definition: Disease-causing, whether the agent is a bacterium, a virus or a fungus. It names the effect on the host, not the kind of organism.
entries.definitionCN: 指能致病的，无论病原是细菌、病毒还是真菌；它命名的是对宿主的作用，而不是生物种类。

entries.definition: Infected with pathogenic bacteria, or relating to such infection. It describes the state of a wound or a blood stream, not the bacteria themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 指被致病细菌感染的，或与这种感染有关的；描述的是伤口或血流所处的状态，而不是细菌本身。

entries.definition: Of or caused by viruses. It is the direct counterpart of bacterial in medical usage and must not be substituted for it.
entries.definitionCN: 指病毒的或由病毒引起的；在医学用法中与 bacterial 直接相对，不可替换使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bacterium + -al: the suffix means 'having to do with', so bacterial is simply 'having to do with bacteria'.
normal.cn: bacterium + -al：后缀意为「与……有关」，所以 bacterial 就是「与细菌有关的」。

normal.en: The name began with a shape: Greek baktērion is a small stick, and the first bacteria seen were rod-shaped.
normal.cn: 这个名字起于形状：希腊语 baktērion 是「小棍」，而最早看到的细菌正是杆状的。

normal.en: One cell is bacterium, two or more are bacteria; the adjective bacterial sidesteps the choice.
normal.cn: 一个细胞是 bacterium，两个及以上是 bacteria；形容词 bacterial 回避了这个选择。

normal.en: The family runs bacterium, bacteria, bacterial, bacterially, bacteriology, bactericidal and antibacterial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 bacterium、bacteria、bacterial、bacterially、bacteriology、bactericidal、antibacterial。

normal.en: Medical pairs fix the meaning: bacterial infection against viral infection; bacterial resistance against antibiotic misuse.
normal.cn: 医学上的成对搭配固定了词义：细菌感染对病毒感染；细菌耐药性对抗生素滥用。

abstract.en: Picture a row of short dashes in a dish, each dash a living cell that splits in two.
abstract.cn: 想象培养皿里一排短横线，每一道都是一个活细胞，正在一分为二。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible army entering a wound, carrying a flag that reads bacterial.
abstract.cn: 想象一支看不见的军队进入伤口，打着写有 bacterial 的旗号。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked 'no entry' that antibiotics can open, while the bacteria behind it keep changing the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着「禁止入内」的门，抗生素本可打开它，而门后的细菌不断换锁。

examples.en: Bacterial contamination forced the plant to recall the whole batch.
examples.cn: 细菌污染迫使工厂召回整批产品。

examples.en: The nurse swabbed the wound to identify the bacterial species involved.
examples.cn: 护士擦拭伤口取样，以确定涉及的细菌种类。

examples.en: Bacterial life survives in hot springs and around deep-sea vents.
examples.cn: 细菌生命在温泉和深海热泉周围依然存活。

root: 希腊 baktron「棍、杖」→ 指小词 baktērion「小棍」→ 现代拉丁 bacterium（1838 年作为科学术语引入，因最早观察到的细菌呈杆状）→ 英语复数 bacteria → 逆构单数 bacterium → 形容词 bacterial（bacterium + -al）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one core, the rod-shaped single cell. The adjective attaches that cell to a structure, a cause, a population, a trait, a community, a contamination or a plant disease.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个核心——杆状单细胞。这个形容词把这细胞分别接到结构、病因、种群、性状、群落、污染与植物病害上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one rod-shaped cell seen through a microscope, alone or in a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下的一根杆状细胞，或单独、或排成一列。

branches.en: CLASS: the bare relation to bacteria as a group, with no further claim.
branches.cn: 类别：只表示与细菌这一类相关，不附加其他断言。

branches.en: CAUSE: a bacterial cause can act on an animal wound or on a plant field; the adjective stays the same while the host changes.
branches.cn: 病因：细菌病因既可作用于动物伤口，也可作用于植物田地；宿主改变，形容词不变。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: the adjective can point to the cell as an object of study rather than to its effects.
branches.cn: 结构：该形容词可以指向作为研究对象的细胞本身，而不是它的影响。

branches.en: POPULATION: growth measures a multiplying population, and flora names a settled community in one place.
branches.cn: 种群：生长量衡量的是不断增殖的种群，菌群则指某处稳定居住的群落。

branches.en: THREAT: resistance is a trait kept by the organism, while contamination is unwanted bacteria entering a substance.
branches.cn: 威胁：耐药性是生物体自身保有的性状，污染则是不需要的细菌进入某物质。

intro.en: Bacterial is a Greek-derived noun turned adjective by a Latin suffix: a root meaning 'stick', a diminutive ending, a Modern Latin noun and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: bacterial 是希腊来源的名词经拉丁后缀变成形容词：表示「棍」的词根、指小词尾、现代拉丁名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin bacterium supplied the noun; Latin -alis supplied the adjective ending. Latin baculum 'rod, staff' is a cognate from the same reconstructed root, not the source of the Greek word.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁 bacterium 提供了名词，拉丁 -alis 提供了形容词词尾。拉丁语 baculum「杆、杖」与希腊词同出同一个重构词根，但并不是希腊词的来源。
